Custom exception class derived from std::exception used to report BrainFlow errors. It stores an exit_code and composes the what() message by concatenating the provided msg and the exit_code. Destructor and what() are marked throw() (noexcept in modern terms).

Configuration struct passed from the user API (often serialized to JSON) containing connection and source parameters for BrainFlow boards and data streams. Fields include serial, MAC, IP endpoints (main/aux/anc), protocol and timeout, optional serial number and file paths, and the target board ID. It provides default initialization and comparison operators to support usage as a map key. BoardIds::NO_BOARD is used as the default master_board; BoardIds enum is declared externally in brainflow_constants.h and not defined here.

Typedef or alias not defined here. The only types in this header are built-in C types (int, char) and macros for linkage/calling convention. There are no custom structs, enums, typedefs, or classes defined in this header. Therefore, there are no custom data types to document.

objects.definition: typedef const struct JNINativeInterface *JNIEnv;
objects.description: Typedef defining JNIEnv as a pointer to a const JNINativeInterface structure, representing the JNI environment handle used when interacting with Java via JNI. This header only creates the alias; the underlying JNINativeInterface struct is not defined here.

Configuration/value object carrying parameters for a BrainFlow model. It includes metric and classifier identifiers plus file/other_info/output_name strings and a max_array_size limit. Provides a custom less-than operator for use as a map key and a two-argument constructor initializing defaults. No explicit destructor or copy/move semantics are defined (implicitly generated).

No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. It only declares a set of C functions exported from a shared library. All parameter and return types used are built-in C types or pointers to built-ins (char*, double*, int*).
Lightweight struct capturing lexer/reader position: total chars read, chars in current line, and number of lines read. Implicitly convertible to size_t (total chars) to preserve SAX interfaces.
Base exception class for the JSON library. Carries an integer id and a message (via std::runtime_error). All library exceptions derive from this.
Exception indicating a parse error (JSON/CBOR/MessagePack/BSON). Provides factory create() helpers and exposes the byte index of the error.
Exception for iterator-related errors (incompatible iterators, out-of-range, wrong container, etc.). Construct via create().
Exception for type mismatches when using JSON API with wrong value types (e.g., using at() on string).
Exception indicating access outside allowed bounds (e.g., index/key not found, excessive sizes, numeric overflow).
Generic exception for errors not covered by parse/type/iterator/out_of_range (e.g., failed JSON Patch test).
Sentinel type used in detection idiom utilities to represent non-existent operations/types.
Enumeration of supported input formats for the binary_reader and parser: textual JSON and various binary encodings.
Low-level input adapter to read bytes from a C FILE* one byte at a time. Used by parser/binary_reader.
Input adapter for std::istream reading, handling BOM and stream state. Reads via streambuf for performance.
Input adapter over a contiguous char buffer and length, returning successive bytes until end.
Wrapper to allow implicit construction of an input_buffer_adapter from pointers/iterators/containers; used so parse({ptr,len}) works.
Internal iterator for primitive JSON types to satisfy iterator interface for scalars. Models begin/end with two states.
Policy for handling invalid UTF-8 during serialization: strict (throw), replace (U+FFFD), or ignore.
Enumeration of all JSON value types used by basic_json and utilities; provides a custom ordering for comparisons.

The main JSON DOM class template implementing a full-featured JSON value with object/array/string/number/bool/binary/null types, parsing/serialization (textual and binary), iterators, JSON Pointer, JSON Patch, diff/merge_patch, etc. Alias nlohmann::json provided.

Concrete C++ class that provides the public API for communicating with BrainFlow-supported boards. It manages session lifecycle (prepare, start/stop stream, release), metadata queries, and data acquisition utilities. Holds BrainFlowInputParams by value and exposes many static helpers. Destructor is trivial; ownership rules and resource cleanup are handled by explicit methods (release_session/stop_stream or release_all_sessions).

A purely static utility class providing signal-processing operations for BrainFlow data, including filtering, spectral analysis, wavelets, ICA/CSP, file I/O helpers, and logging configuration. No constructors or instance state are defined; all methods are static. Ownership of returned heap arrays (e.g., double*, int*, std::complex<double>*) is not documented here and likely requires the caller to manage deallocation externally via the BrainFlow C API or corresponding free functions; details unknown in this header.

Class that wraps machine-learning model lifecycle and logging for BrainFlow. It owns configuration via BrainFlowModelParams and provides static logging controls and global release, plus instance methods to prepare, predict on raw data arrays, and release resources. Destructor is trivial here; details about internal resources and ownership are not shown in this header.

functions.name: product
functions.signature: template <size_t N> static inline int product(const std::array<int, N> &array)
functions.description: Computes the product of all N elements in the given integer array and returns it as an int. Useful for calculating total element counts from a shape array.
requirements: Input array must have exactly N elements (enforced by the template parameter).
No overflow checks are performed; the product is computed using int arithmetic.

functions.name: zero_array
functions.signature: template <size_t N> static inline std::array<int, N> zero_array()
functions.description: Creates and returns an integer array of length N filled with zeros. Used for default-initializing shape/stride arrays.
requirements: None beyond valid instantiation with a non-zero N.

functions.name: make_array
functions.description: Constructs and returns a 1D size array with one element {size0}. Often used to initialize BrainFlowArray shapes.
requirements: None explicitly enforced; negative or zero sizes are not checked here.

functions.name: make_array
functions.signature: static inline std::array<int, 2> make_array(int size0, int size1)
functions.description: Constructs and returns a 2D size array with elements {size0, size1}.
requirements: None explicitly enforced; negative or zero sizes are not checked here.

functions.name: make_array
functions.signature: static inline std::array<int, 3> make_array(int size0, int size1, int size2)
functions.description: Constructs and returns a 3D size array with elements {size0, size1, size2}.
requirements: None explicitly enforced; negative or zero sizes are not checked here.

functions.name: make_stride
functions.signature: template <size_t N> static inline std::array<int, N> make_stride(const std::array<int, N> &size)
functions.description: Computes row-major contiguous strides for a tensor with the given size array: stride[N-1]=1; stride[i]=stride[i+1]*size[i+1].
requirements: Input size array must have exactly N elements (enforced by the template parameter).
No overflow checks are performed; stride values are computed using int arithmetic.
No validation of size values; negative or zero sizes are not checked here.

functions.name: BrainFlowArray::get_item_size
functions.signature: template <typename T, size_t Dim> int BrainFlowArray<T, Dim>::get_item_size() const
functions.description: Returns sizeof(T), i.e., the size in bytes of a single element of the array.

functions.name: BrainFlowArray::get_length
functions.signature: template <typename T, size_t Dim> int BrainFlowArray<T, Dim>::get_length() const
functions.description: Returns the total number of elements in the array (product of its sizes).
requirements: None.

functions.name: BrainFlowArray::get_ndims
functions.signature: template <typename T, size_t Dim> int BrainFlowArray<T, Dim>::get_ndims() const

requirements: None.

functions.name: BrainFlowArray::get_sizes

functions.name: BrainFlowArray::get_size
functions.signature: template <typename T, size_t Dim> int BrainFlowArray<T, Dim>::get_size(int dim) const
functions.description: Returns the size of the specified dimension. Throws BrainFlowException if dim is out of [0, Dim).
requirements: dim must satisfy 0 <= dim < Dim to avoid BrainFlowException with INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR.

functions.name: BrainFlowArray::get_strides
functions.signature: template <typename T, size_t Dim> const std::array<int, Dim> &BrainFlowArray<T, Dim>::get_strides() const
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the per-dimension stride array (row-major contiguous layout).
requirements: Do not store a dangling reference beyond the lifetime of the BrainFlowArray instance.

functions.name: BrainFlowArray::get_stride
functions.signature: template <typename T, size_t Dim> int BrainFlowArray<T, Dim>::get_stride(int dim) const
functions.description: Returns the stride for the specified dimension. No bounds checking is performed.

functions.name: BrainFlowArray::at
functions.signature: template <typename T, size_t Dim> T &BrainFlowArray<T, Dim>::at(int index0)
functions.description: Bounds-checked element access for 1D indexing. Computes flat index index0 * stride(0) and returns a reference. Throws if the computed index is out of range.
requirements: Dim must be >= 1 for this overload to be meaningful (enforced by class usage).
Caller must ensure index0 >= 0 and index0 * get_stride(0) < get_length(); negative indices are not checked and can cause undefined behavior.
Throws BrainFlowException with INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR if computed index >= length.

requirements: Caller must ensure index0 >= 0 and index0 * get_stride(0) < get_length(); negative indices are not checked and can cause undefined behavior.
Throws BrainFlowException with INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR if computed index >= length.

functions.name: BrainFlowArray::at

functions.description: Bounds-checked element access for 2D indexing. Computes flat index index0 * stride(0) + index1 * stride(1) and returns a reference. Throws if out of range.

Caller must ensure index0, index1 are >= 0 and the computed flat index is < get_length(); negative indices are not checked and can cause undefined behavior.
Throws BrainFlowException with INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR if computed index >= length.

functions.description: Const bounds-checked element access for 2D indexing. Computes flat index index0 * stride(0) + index1 * stride(1) and returns a const reference. Throws if out of range.

requirements: ptr must point to a buffer containing at least num elements of type T.
num must be >= 0 and num <= get_length(); no bounds checking is performed.
Array must have a valid allocated buffer (get_raw_ptr() not nullptr) before calling; otherwise behavior is undefined.

functions.description: Streams a textual representation of the array to an output stream, including strides, sizes, and up to 10 elements per dimension (special-cased for 2D). Intended for debugging/logging.
requirements: array must be a valid BrainFlowArray instance; printing an empty array is allowed.
The output stream must be in a good state to accept writes.

functions.name: BrainFlowException::BrainFlowException
functions.description: Constructs a BrainFlowException with a human-readable message and an associated exit code. The constructor builds the internal message by concatenating the provided C-string msg with the decimal string representation of exit_code (no separator). Typically thrown to report errors from a lower-level API and later queried via what() or exit_code.
requirements: msg must point to a valid, null-terminated C string (nullptr is invalid as it is passed to std::string).
exit_code may be any int; no specific range constraints are documented.
The returned what() message will include msg immediately followed by the decimal digits of exit_code without spacing or punctuation.

functions.name: BrainFlowException::~BrainFlowException
functions.description: Destroys the BrainFlowException. Declared with throw() (equivalent to noexcept(true)), so it does not throw exceptions during destruction. Standard RAII cleanup of internal state.
requirements: No special caller requirements; destruction is noexcept and can occur during stack unwinding.

functions.name: BrainFlowException::what
functions.description: Returns a C-string describing the exception. Overrides std::exception::what. The pointer refers to the internal message buffer and remains valid for the lifetime of the BrainFlowException object. Declared throw() (noexcept).
requirements: May be called on a const BrainFlowException object.
Do not free or modify the returned pointer; ownership remains with the exception object.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for arbitrary byte buffers used by several fuzz stubs:
# - BrainFlow config_board_with_bytes expects raw bytes (opaque payload) with a caller-provided length.
# - nlohmann::json binary_t construction uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR converted to bytes. Valid UTF-8 is not required;
#   any 8-bit values are accepted. However, producing a mix of patterns/sizes increases path coverage
#   while remaining valid.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build small-to-moderate buffers (0..256 bytes typical in stubs) comprised of:
#   - printable ASCII segments (for possible string-like handling paths)
#   - binary segments (all 0x00..0xFF, including NULs and high-bytes)
#   - structured subchunks that resemble lengths, counters, or magic tags
#   - optional repetition and edge-case sizes (0, 1, power-of-two, 255, 256)
# - Keep final size <= 4096 (we stay within <= 512 by design).
# - Deterministic randomness based on input seed.

ASCII_SETS: List[bytes] = [
    b"", b"A", b"0", b"\n", b" ", b"!@#", b"test", b"BrainFlow", b"JSON", b"BINARY",
    b"file://out.bin:w", b"streaming_board://239.0.0.1:12345",
]
MAGICS: List[bytes] = [b"BIN\x00", b"RAW\x01", b"CFG\x02", b"\x89BIN\x0D\x0A", b"JF\x01"]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Efficient random bytes
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _edge_lengths(rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    base = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256]
    # Add a couple random lengths in [5, 256]
    for _ in range(4):
        base.append(rng.randint(5, 256))
    # shuffle for diversity
    rng.shuffle(base)
    return base


def _structured_chunk(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Optionally prepend a magic tag
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        parts.append(rng.choice(MAGICS))
    # Include a small header with length and flags-like bytes
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        # 16-bit length value of a following payload (may or may not match actual size, but valid as bytes)
        length_hint = rng.randint(0, 256)
        parts.append(struct.pack('<H', length_hint))
        # flags/subtype-like
        parts.append(struct.pack('B', rng.randint(0, 255)))
    # Add an ASCII segment
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        s = rng.choice(ASCII_SETS)
        # maybe repeat
        rep = rng.randint(1, 3)
        parts.append(s * rep)
    # Add some random binary bytes
    parts.append(_rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 32)))
    return b"".join(parts)


def _build_payload(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Construct a payload up to target_len with mixed segments
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < target_len:
        choice = rng.random()
        remaining = target_len - len(out)
        if choice < 0.25:
            # ASCII only
            seg = rng.choice(ASCII_SETS)
            if not seg:
                seg = b"A"
            seg = (seg * rng.randint(1, 8))[:remaining]
        elif choice < 0.55:
            # random binary
            seg = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, min(32, remaining)))
        elif choice < 0.8:
            # structured chunk
            seg = _structured_chunk(rng)
            if len(seg) > remaining:
                seg = seg[:remaining]
        else:
            # small numeric patterns (counters, repeats)
            kind = rng.randint(0, 2)
            if kind == 0:
                # ascending counter from random start
                start = rng.randint(0, 255)
                n = rng.randint(1, min(32, remaining))
                seg = bytes(((start + i) & 0xFF) for i in range(n))
            elif kind == 1:
                # constant byte fill
                bval = rng.randint(0, 255)
                seg = bytes([bval]) * rng.randint(1, min(32, remaining))
            else:
                # alternating pattern
                a, b = rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(0, 255)
                n = rng.randint(1, min(32, remaining))
                seg = bytes((a if (i & 1) == 0 else b) for i in range(n))
        if not seg:
            continue
        # Limit to remaining
        if len(seg) > remaining:
            seg = seg[:remaining]
        out.extend(seg)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a target size with emphasis on small buffers used by stubs (<=256),
    # but occasionally go larger (up to 512) while still valid.
    sizes = _edge_lengths(rng)
    # Bias towards typical stub maxima
    sizes.extend([rng.randint(0, 64), rng.randint(65, 128), rng.randint(129, 256)])
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        sizes.append(rng.randint(257, 512))
    target_len = rng.choice(sizes)

    # 10% chance to emit empty buffer (valid and exercises len==0 paths)
    if rng.random() < 0.10:
        target_len = 0

    payload = _build_payload(rng, target_len)

    # Ensure total size <= 4096
    if len(payload) > 4096:
        payload = payload[:4096]

    return payload

# Generator for valid filesystem path inputs suitable for functions expecting writable/readable files.
# Strategy:
# - Create short, valid relative paths within current working directory (no I/O performed here).
# - Return bytes containing a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string path or plain path string.
# - Include variations: simple filenames, nested directories (as strings), different extensions, and modes encoded by caller.
# - Keep under 4096 bytes.
# Note: The fuzz harness creates the file at FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME time; we only need to supply a plausible path string.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."
EXTS = [
    "log", "txt", "csv", "dat", "bin", "json", "ml", "model", "out", "tmp"
]
SUBDIRS = [
    ".",  # current directory
    "logs", "output", "data", "tmp", "run", os.path.join("var", "log")
]
PREFIXES = ["bf", "brainflow", "data", "session", "run", "stream", "model"]


def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 4, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n)).strip()


def _pick_ext(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(EXTS)


def _pick_subdir(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Sometimes choose multi-level subdir
    choice = rng.choice(SUBDIRS)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        # append one random component to increase variability
        choice = os.path.join(choice, _rand_name(rng, 3, 8))
    return choice


def _compose_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rng.choice(PREFIXES)
    mid = _rand_name(rng, 3, 10)
    # Add optional timestamp-like number to vary
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        mid += f"_{rng.randint(0, 999999):06d}"
    ext = _pick_ext(rng)
    return f"{base}_{mid}.{ext}"


def _maybe_env_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Occasionally reference system temp or home to vary absolute vs relative paths
    opts: List[str] = []
    tmp = os.getenv("TMPDIR") or os.getenv("TEMP") or os.getenv("TMP")
    if tmp:
        opts.append(tmp)
    home = os.getenv("HOME")
    if home:
        opts.append(os.path.join(home, "tmp"))
        opts.append(os.path.join(home, "logs"))
    if not opts:
        return ""
    return rng.choice(opts)


def _build_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Decide between relative and absolute-like path; relative preferred for sandbox friendliness
    use_abs = rng.random() < 0.2
    parts: List[str] = []

    if use_abs:
        base = _maybe_env_path(rng)
        if not base:
            # fallback to current working directory
            base = os.getcwd()
        parts.append(base)
    else:
        parts.append(_pick_subdir(rng))

    # Optionally add another nested directory
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        parts.append(_rand_name(rng, 3, 10))

    parts.append(_compose_filename(rng))

    path = os.path.join(*parts)

    # Normalize to remove redundant separators
    path = os.path.normpath(path)

    # Ensure it's not empty and within size limits
    if not path:
        path = _compose_filename(rng)

    # Avoid paths that end with a dot or space (problematic on some filesystems)
    path = path.rstrip(" .")
    if not path:
        path = _compose_filename(rng)

    return path


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Generate between 1 and 3 candidate paths and pick one to increase diversity deterministically
    candidates = [_build_path(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
    path = rng.choice(candidates)

    # Return as UTF-8 bytes. FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME expects a C-string; harness will NUL-terminate.
    b = path.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
    if len(b) > 4096:
        # Trim conservatively from the middle if somehow exceeded
        keep = 4096
        b = b[:keep]
        # Ensure we don't cut in the middle of a multibyte sequence: re-decode safely
        path = b.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        b = path.encode("utf-8")
    return b

import json
import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator crafts valid JSON strings expected by the fuzzer stubs and also
# provides plausible filename-like payloads. The returned bytes are meant to seed
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME with useful, valid configurations.
#
# Target stubs expect JSON objects with fields like metric, classifier, file, other_info.
# They also parse arbitrary JSON via nlohmann::json. We therefore return a concatenation
# of several complete JSON texts separated by newlines, plus some filename-looking tokens
# that FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME might pick from the same buffer depending on the harness.
#
# Constraints taken from stubs:
# - metric in [0,2]
# - classifier in [0,2]
# - file: any filename string
# - other_info: any JSON-safe string
# - Overall JSON must be syntactically valid
#
# We include multiple JSON objects covering different combinations and optional fields
# to trigger varied code paths while staying valid.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.:/\\"


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List):
    return seq[rng.randrange(0, len(seq))]


def _rand_string(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, alphabet: str = SAFE_CHARS) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce cross-platform-looking filenames and URIs that the stubs allow (file://, etc.)
    bases = [
        "model.onnx", "model.bin", "weights.dat", "params.json", "pipeline.yml",
        "clf.so", "libclf.dll", "libclf.dylib"
    ]
    dirs = [
        "/tmp/", "/var/tmp/", "/data/models/", "./", "../", "C:/temp/", "C:/models/"
    ]
    schemes = ["file://", "", "file:///", "file://./"]
    # Occasionally add write/append suffix as used in streamer params
    suffixes = ["", ":w", ":a"]
    # Compose
    path = _rand_choice(rng, schemes) + _rand_choice(rng, dirs) + _rand_choice(rng, bases)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        path += _rand_choice(rng, suffixes)
    return path


def _json_params(rng: random.Random, with_file: bool) -> dict:
    obj = {
        "metric": rng.randrange(0, 3),
        "classifier": rng.randrange(0, 3),
        # Keep other_info JSON-string friendly: avoid quotes/newlines
        "other_info": _rand_string(rng, 0, 48, alphabet=string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-:/.,")
    }
    if with_file:
        obj["file"] = _rand_filename(rng)
    # Optionally include extra benign fields some consumers may ignore but JSON parser handles
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        obj["output_name"] = _rand_string(rng, 3, 16)
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        obj["max_array_size"] = rng.choice([256, 1024, 4096, 8192])
    return obj


def _json_roundtrip_payloads(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Objects crafted to exercise generic JSON parsing and streaming operator>>
    payloads = []
    # Simple object with mixed types
    payloads.append(json.dumps({
        "k1": 1,
        "k2": _rand_string(rng, 0, 24),
        "nested": {"a": True, "b": None, "c": [1, 2, 3]},
    }, separators=(",", ":")))
    # Array payload
    payloads.append(json.dumps([
        {"s": _rand_string(rng, 0, 12)},
        {"n": int(rng.getrandbits(31))},
        {"b": rng.choice([True, False])}
    ], separators=(",", ":")))
    # Numbers and strings edge-ish cases
    payloads.append(json.dumps({
        "s": _rand_string(rng, 0, 64),
        "n": int(rng.getrandbits(31)) * rng.choice([1, -1])
    }, separators=(",", ":")))
    return payloads


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a set of valid JSON parameter blobs used by prepare/predict/release
    objs: List[dict] = []
    # Ensure coverage: with and without file field
    for with_file in [True, False, True]:
        objs.append(_json_params(rng, with_file))

    # Diversify metric/classifier combinations at boundaries
    objs.append({"metric": 0, "classifier": 0, "other_info": "baseline", "file": _rand_filename(rng)})
    objs.append({"metric": 2, "classifier": 2, "other_info": "max", "file": _rand_filename(rng)})

    json_texts = [json.dumps(o, separators=(",", ":")) for o in objs]

    # Add several filename tokens alone as separate lines for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME consumers
    filenames = [
        _rand_filename(rng),
        _rand_filename(rng),
        "file://" + _rand_string(rng, 3, 8) + ".dat",
        "./" + _rand_string(rng, 3, 8) + ".bin",
    ]

    # Add general JSONs to exercise nlohmann::json parsing and operator>> round-trips
    json_texts.extend(_json_roundtrip_payloads(rng))

    # Compose the buffer: newline-delimited records so that consumers reading tokens get whole items
    records: List[str] = []
    # Interleave to improve variety
    for i in range(max(len(json_texts), len(filenames))):
        if i < len(json_texts):
            records.append(json_texts[i])
        if i < len(filenames):
            records.append(filenames[i])

    # Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes; trim if necessary by dropping tail records
    encoded = "\n".join(records).encode("utf-8")
    if len(encoded) > 4096:
        # Drop from the end until under limit
        while records and len("\n".join(records).encode("utf-8")) > 4096:
            records.pop()
        encoded = "\n".join(records).encode("utf-8")

    return encoded
